about: Change index: what changed in Minecraft between neighbouring releases, in Mojang's official names, with families, hubs, rule coverage and the best recorded port per step. Generated by tools/ChangeIndex.java and bench/change_routes.py.
counting: Counts in each step file are per listed change. 'Api' counts leave out private members. breakingShare = (classes removed or renamed + non-private methods and fields removed, renamed or with a new signature, including those of removed classes) / (classes + non-private methods and fields of the older release).

linked.exact: Both releases are obfuscated and joined through Fabric intermediary ids: a rename is proven by the shared id.
linked.by-name: At least one release ships unobfuscated (26.1+), so there is no shared id: classes and members are matched by name, and renames and moves are best guesses (same simple name, nested classes that moved together, half or more member names shared, or one member on each side with the same signature).

families.rule: A new family starts at any update that breaks at least 1 in 100 of the game's names (classes, methods and fields a mod can call that were removed, renamed or given a new signature). Updates inside a family break fewer than 1 in 200. Measured over every release from 1.14.4, no update falls between 0.5% and 1.1%, so the line sits in a natural gap rather than at a chosen round number.
families.hubRule: Each family's hub is the release in it with the most mods on Modrinth (counted on the date shown), because a port that starts or ends there helps the most people. A family of one release is its own hub.

routing: Route from X to Y: neighbouring steps from X to its family's hub, then hub to hub, then neighbouring steps from the last hub to Y. A backport walks the same steps in reverse (added and removed swap, renames flip). A step inside a family breaks under 0.5% of names.
matching: A change counts as handled by the mappings when the two releases are linked by Fabric's intermediary ids (every release up to 1.21.11) and the change is a rename or a move: port --fix rewrites those imports and call sites from the generated map. A change into 26.1 or later has no shared id, so nothing there is counted as mapped.

A change counts as handled by a rule when a rule in knowledge/ applies to that update (its jump range covers it) and names the change: for a rename the rule's old side names the old name and its new side the new name; for a removal or a new signature the rule's old side names the member (names shorter than six letters also need the class name). This is matching by name and is approximate: a rule can name a method without fixing every use of it.

Automatic rules are knowledge/fixes.json (applied by port --fix) and knowledge/renames.json. A written how-to is a note in knowledge/version-changes.json or knowledge/structural.json that names the change: it explains what to do and shows in the port report, but nothing is edited for you.
Rules written in yarn names (knowledge/learned and fixes marked yarn) are not compared: the index uses Mojang's names, and the two only sometimes agree.

mods.note: Mods per release on Modrinth (project_type:mod, any loader).
